{{short description|Algebraic variety that is a moduli space for principally polarized abelian varieties}}
[[File:CalabiYau5.jpg|thumb|A 2D slice of a [[Calabi–Yau manifold|Calabi–Yau]] quintic. One such quintic is birationally equivalent to the compactification of the Siegel modular variety ''A''<sub>1,3</sub>(2).<ref name="survey"/>]]

In mathematics, a '''Siegel modular variety''' or '''Siegel moduli space''' is an [[algebraic variety]] that parametrizes certain types of [[abelian variety|abelian varieties]] of a fixed [[Dimension of an algebraic variety|dimension]]. More precisely, Siegel modular varieties are the [[moduli space]]s of [[Abelian variety#Polarisations|principally polarized abelian varieties]] of a fixed dimension. They are named after [[Carl Ludwig Siegel]], the 20th-century German [[number theory|number theorist]] who introduced the varieties in 1943.<ref name="Oda">{{cite book|chapter=Intersections of Two Walls of the Gottschling Fundamental Domain of the Siegel Modular Group of Genus Two |last=Oda |first=Takayuki |pages=193–221 |title=Automorphic Forms, Research in Number Theory from Oman |editor1-last=Heim |editor1-first=Bernhard |editor2-last=Al-Baali |editor2-first=Mehiddin |editor3-last=Rupp |editor3-first=Florian |series=Springer Proceedings in Mathematics & Statistics |volume=115 |publisher=Springer |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-11352-4_15 |isbn=978-3-319-11352-4 |year=2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Symplectic Geometry |last=Siegel |first=Carl Ludwig |journal=American Journal of Mathematics |volume=65 |issue=1 |year=1943 |pages=1–86 |doi=10.2307/2371774 |publisher=The Johns Hopkins University Press|jstor=2371774 }}</ref>

Siegel modular varieties are the most basic examples of [[Shimura variety|Shimura varieties]].<ref name="Milne">{{cite book|chapter=Introduction to Shimura Varieties |last=Milne |first=James S. |authorlink=James Milne (mathematician) |title= Harmonic Analysis, the Trace Formula, and Shimura Varieties |editor1-last=Arthur |editor1-first=James |editor2-last=Ellwood |editor2-first=David |editor3-last=Kottwitz |editor3-first=Robert |publisher=American mathematical Society and Clay Mathematics Institute |series=Clay Mathematics Proceedings |volume=4 |isbn=978-0-8218-3844-0 |chapter-url=http://www.claymath.org/library/proceedings/cmip04.pdf |pages=265–378 |year=2005}}</ref> Siegel modular varieties generalize [[moduli of algebraic curves|moduli spaces of elliptic curves]] to higher dimensions and play a central role in the theory of [[Siegel modular form]]s, which generalize classical [[modular form]]s to higher dimensions.<ref name="survey"/> They also have applications to [[black hole thermodynamics|black hole entropy]] and [[conformal field theory]].<ref name="entropy"/>

==Construction==
The Siegel modular variety ''A''<sub>''g''</sub>, which parametrize principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension ''g'', can be constructed as the [[complex analytic space]]s constructed as the [[Geometric quotient|quotient]] of the [[Siegel upper half-space]] of degree ''g'' by the action of a [[symplectic group]]. Complex analytic spaces have naturally associated algebraic varieties by [[Jean-Pierre Serre|Serre]]'s [[Algebraic geometry and analytic geometry#GAGA|GAGA]].<ref name="survey">{{cite book |last1=Hulek |first1=Klaus |author-link=Klaus Hulek |title=Higher Dimensional Birational Geometry |last2=Sankaran |first2=G. K. |volume=35 |year=2002 |pages=89–156 |doi=10.2969/aspm/03510089 |arxiv=math/9810153 |chapter-url=https://projecteuclid.org/download/pdf_1/euclid.aspm/1546230378 |isbn=978-4-931469-85-3 |chapter=The Geometry of Siegel Modular Varieties  |series=Advanced Studies in Pure Mathematics|s2cid=119595519 }}</ref>

The Siegel modular variety ''A''<sub>''g''</sub>(''n''), which parametrize principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension ''g'' with a [[Level structure (algebraic geometry)|level ''n''-structure]], arises as the quotient of the Siegel upper half-space by the action of the [[Congruence subgroup#Congruence subgroups|principal congruence subgroup]] of level ''n'' of a symplectic group.<ref name="survey"/>

A Siegel modular variety may also be constructed as a Shimura variety defined by the Shimura datum associated to a [[symplectic vector space]].<ref name="Milne"/>

==Properties==
The Siegel modular variety ''A''<sub>''g''</sub> has dimension ''g''(''g''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1)/2.<ref name="survey"/><ref>{{cite book |chapter=The cohomology of the moduli space of Abelian varieties |last=van der Geer |first=Gerard |title=The Handbook of Moduli, Volume 1 |editor1-first=Gavril |editor1-last=Farkas |editor2-first=Ian |editor2-last=Morrison |volume=24 |year=2013 |publisher=International Press |location=Somerville, Mass. |isbn=9781571462572 |arxiv=1112.2294}}</ref> Furthermore, it was shown by Yung-Sheng Tai, [[Eberhard Freitag]], and [[David Mumford]] that ''A<sub>g</sub>'' is of [[Kodaira dimension#General type|general type]] when ''g''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;7.<ref name="survey"/><ref>{{cite journal |first=Yung-Sheng |last=Tai |title=On the Kodaira dimension of the moduli space of abelian varieties |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |volume=68 |issue=3 |year=1982 |pages=425–439|doi=10.1007/BF01389411 |url=https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/id/PPN356556735_0068?tify=%7B%22view%22:%22info%22,%22pages%22:%5B431%5D%7D|bibcode=1982InMat..68..425T |s2cid=120441933 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |first=Eberhard |last=Freitag |title=Siegelsche Modulfunktionen |volume=254 |language=de |publisher=Springer-Verlag |year=1983|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-68649-8|series=Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften |isbn=978-3-642-68650-4 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|first=David |last=Mumford |chapter=On the Kodaira dimension of the Siegel modular variety |title=Algebraic Geometry - Open Problems, Proceedings of the Conference held in Ravello, May 31 - June 5, 1982 |editor1-first= C. |editor1-last=Ciliberto |editor2-first= F. |editor2-last=Ghione |editor3-first= F. |editor3-last=Orecchia |pages=348–375 |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |volume=997 |publisher=Springer |year=1983|doi=10.1007/BFb0061652|isbn=978-3-540-12320-0 }}</ref>

Siegel modular varieties can be compactified to obtain [[projective variety|projective varieties]].<ref name="survey"/> In particular, a compactification of ''A''<sub>2</sub>(2) is [[Birational geometry#Birational maps|birationally equivalent]] to the [[Segre cubic]] which is in fact [[rational variety|rational]].<ref name="survey"/> Similarly, a compactification of ''A''<sub>2</sub>(3) is birationally equivalent to the [[Burkhardt quartic]] which is also rational.<ref name="survey"/> Another Siegel modular variety, denoted ''A''<sub>1,3</sub>(2), has a compactification that is birationally equivalent to the [[Barth–Nieto quintic]] which is birationally equivalent to a modular [[Calabi–Yau manifold]] with [[Kodaira dimension]] zero.<ref name="survey"/>

Siegel modular varieties cannot be [[anabelian]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Ihara |first1=Yasutaka |author-link=Yasutaka Ihara |title=Geometric Galois Actions 1: Around Grothendieck's Esquisse d'un Programme |last2=Nakamura |first2=Hiroaki |editor-last1 = Schneps |editor-first1  = Leila |editor-link1  = Leila Schneps |editor-last2  = Lochak |editor-first2  = Pierre |editor-link2  = Pierre Lochak |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=1997 |series=London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series |volume=242 |pages=127–138 |chapter=Some illustrative examples for anabelian geometry in high dimensions |doi=10.1017/CBO9780511758874.010|isbn=978-0-521-59642-8 }}</ref>

==Applications==
Siegel modular forms arise as [[vector-valued differential form]]s on Siegel modular varieties.<ref name="survey"/> Siegel modular varieties have been used in conformal field theory via the theory of Siegel modular forms.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Belin |first1=Alexandre |last2=Castro |first2=Alejandra |last3=Gomes |first3=João |last4=Keller |first4=Christoph A. |title=Siegel paramodular forms and sparseness in AdS3/CFT2 |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |date=7 November 2018 |volume=2018 |issue=11 |pages=37 |doi=10.1007/JHEP11(2018)037|arxiv=1805.09336 |bibcode=2018JHEP...11..037B |s2cid=54936474 }}</ref> In [[string theory]], the function that naturally captures the microstates of black hole entropy in the D1D5P system of [[Extremal black hole|supersymmetric black hole]]s is a Siegel modular form.<ref name="entropy">{{cite journal |last1=Belin |first1=Alexandre |last2=Castro |first2=Alejandra |last3=Gomes |first3=João |last4=Keller |first4=Christoph A. |title=Siegel modular forms and black hole entropy|url=https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007%2FJHEP04%282017%29057.pdf |journal=Journal of High Energy Physics |date=11 April 2017 |volume=2017 |issue=4 |pages=57 |doi=10.1007/JHEP04(2017)057|arxiv=1611.04588|bibcode=2017JHEP...04..057B |s2cid=53684898 }} See Section 1 of the paper.</ref>

In 1968, [[Aleksei Parshin]] showed that the [[Faltings' theorem|Mordell conjecture]] (now known as Faltings' theorem) would hold if the [[Igor Shafarevich|Shafarevich]] finiteness conjecture was true by introducing Parshin's trick.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Algebraic curves over function fields I|last=Parshin|first=A. N.|authorlink=Aleksei Parshin|journal=[[Izvestiya: Mathematics|Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR Ser. Mat.]]|volume=32|issue=5|year=1968|pages=1191–1219|url=http://www.mathnet.ru/links/122f62ba321659ce3eb4902db899ab61/im2513.pdf|bibcode=1968IzMat...2.1145P|doi=10.1070/IM1968v002n05ABEH000723}}</ref><ref name="Cornell-Silverman"/> In 1983 and 1984, [[Gerd Faltings]] completed the proof of the Mordell conjecture by proving the Shafarevich finiteness conjecture.<ref>{{cite journal |authorlink=Gerd Faltings| last=Faltings |first=Gerd |year=1983 |title=Endlichkeitssätze für abelsche Varietäten über Zahlkörpern |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |volume=73 |issue=3 |pages=349–366 |doi=10.1007/BF01388432 | mr=0718935 | trans-title=Finiteness theorems for abelian varieties over number fields | language=de |url=https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/id/PPN356556735_0073?tify=%7B%22view%22:%22info%22,%22pages%22:%5B355%5D%7D| bibcode=1983InMat..73..349F | s2cid=121049418 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Faltings |first=Gerd |year=1984 |title=Erratum: Endlichkeitssätze für abelsche Varietäten über Zahlkörpern |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |volume=75 |issue=2 |pages=381 |doi=10.1007/BF01388572 | mr=0732554 | language=de |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Cornell-Silverman">{{cite book|title=Arithmetic geometry. Papers from the conference held at the University of Connecticut, Storrs, Connecticut, July 30 – August 10, 1984 |editor1-last=Cornell | editor1-first=Gary | editor2-link=Joseph Hillel Silverman| editor2-last=Silverman | editor2-first=Joseph H. |year=1986 |publisher=Springer-Verlag |location= New York |isbn=0-387-96311-1 | doi=10.1007/978-1-4613-8655-1 | mr=861969}}</ref> The main idea of Faltings' proof is the comparison of [[Height function#Faltings height|Faltings heights]] and [[Height function#Naive height|naive heights]] via Siegel modular varieties.<ref>"Faltings relates the two notions of height by means of the Siegel moduli space.... It is the main idea of the proof." {{cite journal |last=Bloch |first=Spencer |authorlink=Spencer Bloch |page=44 |url=http://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/b509/4b4b6f31976173c38813428be512f7d35c9c.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190303115211/http://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/b509/4b4b6f31976173c38813428be512f7d35c9c.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=2019-03-03 |title=The Proof of the Mordell Conjecture |journal=The Mathematical Intelligencer |volume=6 |issue=2 |year=1984|doi=10.1007/BF03024155 |s2cid=306251 }}</ref>
